headlines.title: San Jose police officer injured in shootout released from hospital
headlines.description: SJPD confirmed Saturday the officer injured during a shootout at a home on Tuesday was released from the hospital. The shootout happened in a home near Tamien Park. Police first spotted a Stolen Chevy Tahoe associated with two recent armed robberies. After a short chase the suspect, identified as Anthony Chavez, crashed into multiple cars before running into a home while a family was inside. Police got the family out and found Chavez hiding in a bathroom. That’s when they say Chavez immediately started shooting at officers, injuring Sergeant Matt Walsh. Walsh and another officer returned fire, ultimately killing Chavez. San Jose Aug 26 San Jose Aug 27 San Jose Aug 25 San Jose police officer injured, suspect killed following shootout

headlines.title: Downtown San Jose celebrates Silicon Valley PRIDE festival
headlines.description: The annual Silicon Valley PRIDE Festival was in full swing in downtown San Jose Saturday. This is the 51st year for the two-day event, ending with the grand parade Sunday. Organizers say what’s different this year is that there’s not just one concert but hours of music and an entire festival in this plaza. The theme this year is flourish and bloom, celebrating strength, resilience, and a vibrant spirit. It’s also an important place to connect during a time when some feel under attack. DJs Al Tego and Noodles were expected to be performing. Attendees can shop at booths, talk to community groups, or just enjoy food and dance. This is designed to be a very family-friendly celebration. Many attendees said they felt it was important San Jose had its own pride festival in addition to what San Francisco offers. The celebration does not end on Saturday; on Sunday, the Silicon Valley Pride Parade will start at 10:30 a.m. on Market Street.

headlines.title: Plaskett Fire prompts new evacuations, more Timber Fire evacuations possible
headlines.description: New evacuation orders and evacuation warnings were issued on Saturday due to the Plaskett Fire burning in Monterey County, authorities said. This comes as fire crews also battle the Timber Fire, further north in Monterey County, where officials warned some Carmel Valley residents that more evacuation orders could be issued later this week. According to Cal Fire, the Plaskett Fire was reported on Wednesday, a few weeks after the Timber Fire erupted on Aug. 8. Both wildfires are burning along the Big Sur coast, with the Plaskett Fire burning 8,241 acres with 0% containment and the Timber Fire burning 24,601 acres and 21% containment as of Saturday afternoon. On Saturday, at around 3 p.m., the United States Army Garrison – Fort Hunger Ligget issued an evacuation order for zone MRY-G012-A and an evacuation warning for the zones MRY-G011-A and MRY-G012-B. Hours earlier, the Monterey County Sheriff’s Office issued an evacuation order for the zone MRY-F037 and an evacuation warning for the zones RY-F038 and MRY-F039. At least one structure was destroyed in the Plaskett Fire. For more information, visit the county’s emergency alerts website. As of Saturday evening, CAL FIRE said that steep terrain and lots of fuel for the fire “continue to create significant challenges for suppression efforts” on the Timber Fire, adding that fire spread is expected toward the Lucia Range, South Fork Trail and the Black Cone Trail. Big Sur resident Jessica Swan said she can see the Timber Fire from where she lives, and the flames can look intimidating, especially when “the winds pick up, and you see those big trees catch on fire.” “We are talking about 200-foot flames, it looks like,” she noted. Swan lives in one of the areas that is under a shelter-in-place order due to the fire. “I’m up here for maybe a week, it could keep going,” she noted. “You know everyone’s prepared with food and water if you were to go down to the highway, it’s just police and fire trucks.” Highway 1 is closed off near Swan in Big Sur as well as further south near the Plaskett Fire. Evacuation shelters have been designated for the Timber and Plaskett Fires at Carmel Mission Inn Conference Room, 3665 Rio Road in Carmel, and at Cambria Veterans Memorial Building in Cambria.

headlines.title: San Francisco authorities focus on safety at PokémonXP
headlines.description: San Francisco is hosting one of the biggest weekends in the Pokémon franchise’s history. With some collectibles worth thousands of dollars, there’s another battle happening behind the scenes: keeping it all safe. Thousands of fans, competitors and collectors from around the world gathered at the Pokémon XP and the World Championships in San Francisco. For many of the fans, the events also mean a lot of shopping. “My total at Pokémon Center for San Francisco was $1,119,” Washington resident Austin Reno said. “I brought about $8,000 of cards to trade and sell.” That’s why safety is serious business this weekend in San Francisco. San Francisco Aug 28 San Francisco Giants Aug 27 San Francisco Aug 27 Some of the most coveted cards at Aloha Card Shop’s booth can fetch five, even six figures; with big money, comes bigger risks. “Especially nowadays with all the money coming into the hobby, there’s a lot of ne’er-do-wells looking for a quick buck, so you really have to be vigilant. We’ve had people steal from us in the past because there’s so much going on and it’s easy to let something slip,” Aloha Card Shop Co-Owner Reece Felix said. Ali Reid has the full report in the video above.

headlines.title: Attempted murder suspect arrested in East Palo Alto
headlines.description: On Saturday, several law enforcement agencies teamed up to arrest an attempted murder suspect in East Palo Alto. Authorities say the suspect led officers on a chase that ended in the Bay, at the Ravenswood Preserve. This prompted a response from East Palo Alto police, San Mateo County deputies, a CHP chopper, and an airboat crew from the Menlo Park Fire District. Once brought out of the water, the suspect was treated by paramedics. Police say the man was wanted for a shooting back in April.

headlines.title: Dozens of animals find new homes at adoption event in the South Bay
headlines.description: On Saturday, dozens of animals found new homes at one of the adoption events happening in the Bay Area. Since 2015, NBC Bay Area and Telemundo 48 have been helping clear animal shelters across the Bay Area during the entire month of August. This is part of the stations’ Clear the Shelters campaign, which has helped more than 1.3 million pets find new homes and raised more than $5.6 million to help support shelters and their public outreach efforts. Employees from NBC Bay Area and Telemundo 48 return and bring home their own furry forever friends, and every year they return to help raise awareness about the issues facing our local shelters. At the Santa Clara County Animal Shelter, dozens of animals found their forever homes, including a puppy named Jessica. Miguel Paredes, a first-time pet owner, adopted a puppy named Chris Chmura. “I’ve always really loved dogs, and this is my first time getting one, so I’m really excited, and I want to give him all the love I can,” Paredes said. NBC Bay Area anchor Audrey Asistio also welcomed a new furry family member with a familiar name. “I can’t believe we adopted Audrey Asistio. We’re going to have to change your name baby girl,” Asistio said. Today in the Bay anchors Laura Garcia and Marcus Washington were at Berkeley Humane with reporter Bob Redell and others. Berkeley Humane was hosting its annual Bark (and Meow) Around the Block adoption event. Billed as California’s largest single adoption event, with live music and food, it attracts thousands of participants and every year hundreds of cats, dogs, rabbits and other animals find new homes during the Clear The Shelters month. “We’ll essentially be doing an adoption every two minutes, which is a huge number of animals going into homes, and that’s important, because the shelters are very full right now, and for every animal that is adopted today, we make more room in the rescues and the shelters for other animals that need the support that they can provide,” Berkeley Humane Executive Director Jeffery Zerwekh said. Clear The Shelters helped more than 160,000 pets get adopted nationwide in 2025 and raised nearly $630,000 for shelters. Over the past 12 years, the local donations have helped immensely. “Because we’ve been able to fund raise a little more than $1 million from what I understand, and that might not sound like a lot to folks, but it means quite a bit to us when we run this shelter,” District One Santa Clara County Board of Supervisors VP Sylvia Arenas said. More than 30 shelters are taking part in the Bay Area and more than 300 pets are expected to find new homes.

headlines.title: Woman dies after being stabbed in San Jose
headlines.description: A woman died after being stabbed in San Jose Friday, the police department said Saturday. Police said they responded to a report of a suspicious circumstance at around 1:50 p.m. in the 700 block of Linda Vista Street. At the scene, officers found an unconscious and unresponsive woman with unknown injuries inside a home, authorities said. The police department said the woman was pronounced dead at the scene. Evidence at the scene determined the woman suffered from at least one stab wound, according to authorities. Authorities said it was determined the suspect, another woman, and the victim knew each other, but added the motive and circumstances surrounding the incident are under investigation.

headlines.title: Bay Area community joins in prayer for those impacted by Nepal floods
headlines.description: On Friday, a Bay Area community came together to pray for those caught in the devastating flooding along the border of Nepal and China’s Tibet region. Dozens gathered at the Nepali Community Center in Richmond to light up candles and pray for families caught in the catastrophic flooding along the border between Nepal and China’s Tibet region. Nepali authorities say 626 people have died, and 2,426 others remain missing. The flooding has devastated communities along the border leaving families across the region desperately searching for news. natural disasters Aug 27 natural disasters Aug 28 milpitas Aug 27 The Nepali Association of Northern California says several of its members have family in the area. Although most have heard from their loved ones, the group says one family is still waiting. The community is also racing to help survivors by raising money for relief and trying to figure out how to get critical supplies into an area where so much of the infrastructure has been destroyed. “Since the bridges are all gone and there is flooding in the rivers, it’s hard for the people to really get there and help the people in need so there are helicopters but there not enough and even the medical kits we are running tight on those,” Nepali Association of Northern California President Preetesh Karki said. In the Bay Area, community members say the Nepali community is not the only community hoping to hear from loved ones who remain missing, as some Tibetan and Indian residents also share that wait. People in the U.S. looking for information about family members in the region are being asked to contact the state department.

headlines.title: 49ers wanted to review police report before disclosing Shanahan crash, records show
headlines.description: Newly released public records are providing a clearer timeline of the communications between the San Francisco 49ers and Palo Alto police after the car crash that seriously injured head coach Kyle Shanahan. The records, first released to the Mercury News, are in response to a public records request NBC Bay Area filed and obtained Friday. The documents help explain why the 49ers waited 11 days to publicly disclose the June 14 crash. Two days after the crash, 49ers Security Director Larry Day emailed a police administrative assistant. Day requested the collision report and information about the other vehicle. Police provided information about the second vehicle that morning, but said the collision report was not yet complete. Six days later, Day followed up. When police told him they were checking the report’s status, Day responded: “We just wanted to review the report today before we release any information to the media.” Police notified the team on July 23 that the report was available. Kyle Shanahan Jul 28 Kyle Shanahan Jul 28 49ers Jul 27 The following day, a text to a police lieutenant from 49ers vice president of security, Jeremy Jones, states he needed to give the department “a heads up on our media release.” The 49ers issued their public statement the next morning. Days later, Jones texted police again after a state database incorrectly listed the other driver as responsible. A lieutenant responded: “I found the problem. We are fixing it.” Police later publicly confirmed Shanahan caused the crash. Shanahan has said he took his eyes off the road to retrieve a dropped cellphone and crossed into oncoming traffic. Palo Alto police have refused to publicly release the crash report that they gave the 49ers, saying only people who are “parties” to the crash can get the report. They told the Mercury News they released it to the Niners because they own the Tesla Shanahan was driving, so they are parties to the crash. Neither Palo Alto police nor the 49ers returned NBC Bay Area’s calls on Friday for comment.

headlines.title: Groups call on South Bay leaders to do more to help homeless population
headlines.description: Twenty community groups have signed an open letter to Santa Clara County and the city of San Jose demanding more be done to assist the unhoused population. The groups say the Here4You hotline isn’t connecting unhoused residents with services efficiently. They also want an end to encampment sweeps until there is adequate housing available, clearer communication on resources, as well as additional therapists and case managers. “You can’t move on to an apartment or anything if there’s not a case manager for you, and you can’t get mental health services if there’s no therapy,” Unhoused Response Group founder Shaunn Cartwright said. Separately, the groups claim that, according to the coroner’s website, the county is on pace to match last year’s homeless population death toll, saying 99 people have already died on the streets this year. Santa Clara County Board of Supervisors President Otto Lee said he’d like to prioritize more short-term housing right away. “That’s 99 people living in our community that could not survive, and that shows that our system is falling short,” he said. Matching last year’s homeless death rate would still mean a lower total than previous years.

headlines.title: Police investigating shooting at San Francisco's Mission Bay neighborhood
headlines.description: Police were investigating a shooting in San Francisco. The shooting was reported 4:17 p.m. Friday at Fourth and Channel streets in the Mission Bay neighborhood. When officers arrived at the scene they found a male juvenile suffering from a gunshot wound, authorities said. The victim was taken to a hospital for non-life threatening injuries. No arrests have been made and no other information was immediately available. Anyone with information is asked to contact the SFPD at 415-575-4444 or text a tip to Tip411 and begin the message with SFPD.

headlines.title: Woman dies after hit-and-run crash in parking lot in Milpitas
headlines.description: A woman died after a hit-and-run crash in a parking lot in Milpitas Friday, according to the police department. Police said the crash was reported just after noon in the parking lot of Mill Creek Apartments, located at 440 Dixon Landing Road. Officials said witnesses reported seeing a blue SUV leaving the area immediately after the incident. Authorities said responding officers found a woman who had sustained significant injuries as a result of the crash. The woman was pronounced dead at the scene, police said. When searching the surrounding area, police said they found a blue SUV matching the witnesses’ description in a nearby parking lot. The vehicle also had significant damage consistent with being involved in a crash, according to authorities. The police department said the driver, a 32-year-old Milpitas resident, was arrested in connection with the incident. Authorities said this is an ongoing investigation.
